sentences.en: In 1885, a 22-year-old Dutch woman named Johanna Boer met Theo van Gogh, the younger brother of the

sentences.zh: 艺术家的弟弟，当时正作为巴黎的一名艺术品经纪人崭露头角。

sentences.en: History knows Theo as the steadier of the van Gogh brothers, the archetypal emotional anchor who selflessly managed Vincent's erratic path through life.
sentences.zh: 历史将西奥视作梵高兄弟中更沉稳的那一个，他是那个无私地应对文森特一生中反常轨迹的典型情感支柱。

sentences.en: Yeo, as she called herself, was raised in a sober, middle-class family.
sentences.zh: 自称为尤的她，在一个清心寡欲的中产阶级家庭中长大。

sentences.en: There is a Dutch maxim, the tallest nail gets hammered down, that the Boer family seems to have taken as gospel.
sentences.zh: 有一句荷兰格言，出头的钉子先挨锤，博尔家族似乎把这奉为圭臬。

sentences.en: Yeo had set herself up in a safely unexciting career as an English teacher in

sentences.en: Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 职业。

sentences.en: She wasn't inclined to impulsiveness.
sentences.zh: 她并不倾向于冲动。

sentences.en: Besides, she was already dating somebody.
sentences.zh: 况且，她已经在和某人约会了。

sentences.en: She said no.
sentences.zh: 她拒绝了。

sentences.en: But Theo persisted.
sentences.zh: 但西奥坚持不懈。

sentences.en: He was attractive in a soulful kind of way, a thinner, paler version of his brother.
sentences.zh: 他有一种深沉迷人的特质，是他的哥哥一个更瘦、更苍白的版本。

sentences.en: Beyond that, she had a taste for culture, a desire to be in the company of artists and intellectuals, which he could certainly provide.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，她对文化有着爱好，渴望与艺术家和知识分子为伍，而这正是他绝对能够提供的。

sentences.en: Eventually, he won her over.
sentences.zh: 最终，他赢得了她的芳心。

sentences.en: In 1888, a year and a half after his proposal, she agreed to marry him.
sentences.zh: 1888年，在他求婚一年半后，她答应嫁给他。

sentences.en: After that, a new life opened up for her.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，一个新的人生为她拉开序幕。

sentences.en: It was Paris, in the Belle Epoque, art, theater, intellectuals, the streets of their Pigalle neighborhood, raucous with cafés and brothels.
sentences.zh: 那是美好年代的巴黎，有艺术、戏剧、知识分子，还有皮加尔街区充斥着咖啡馆和妓院的喧闹街道。

sentences.en: Theo was not just any art dealer.
sentences.zh: 西奥可不仅仅是个普通的艺术品经纪人。

sentences.en: He was at the forefront, specializing in the breed of young artists who were defying the stony realism imposed by the

sentences.zh: 美术学院强加的冷硬现实主义的年轻艺术家群体。

sentences.en: Most dealers wouldn't touch the Impressionists, but they were Theo van Gogh's clients and heroes.
sentences.zh: 大多数经纪人对印象派避之不及，但他们却是西奥·梵高的客户和英雄。

sentences.en: And here they came, Gauguin and Passaro and Toulouse-Lautrec, the young men of the avant-garde, marching through her life with the exotic ferocity of zoo creatures.
sentences.zh: 他们接踵而至，高更、毕沙罗和图卢兹-洛特雷克，这群前卫派的年轻人，带着动物园猛兽般的异国凶猛闯入她的生活。

sentences.en: Yeoh realized that she was in the midst of a movement, that she was witnessing a change in the direction of things.
sentences.zh: 尤意识到自己正置身于一场运动之中，她正在见证事物发展方向的改变。

sentences.en: At home, too, she was feeling fully alive.
sentences.zh: 在家里，她也感到自己完全焕发了生机。

sentences.en: On their marriage night, which she described as blissful, her husband thrilled her by whispering into her ear, wouldn't you like to have a baby, my baby?
sentences.zh: 在他们的洞房花烛夜，她将其描述为无比幸福，她的丈夫在她耳边呢喃，难道你不想生个孩子吗，我的孩子，这让她兴奋不已。

sentences.en: She was powerfully in love, with Theo, with Paris, with life.
sentences.zh: 她深深地坠入爱河，爱着西奥，爱着巴黎，爱着生活。

sentences.en: Theo talked incessantly of their future, and also of things like pigment and color and light, encouraging her to develop a new way of seeing.
sentences.zh: 西奥喋喋不休地谈论着他们的未来，也谈论着颜料、色彩和光线之类的事物，鼓励她培养一种全新的观察方式。

sentences.en: But one subject dominated.
sentences.zh: 但有一个主题占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: From their first meeting, he regaled Yeoh with accounts of his brother's tortured genius.
sentences.zh: 从他们第一次见面起，他就向尤滔滔不绝地讲述他哥哥饱受折磨的天才故事。

sentences.zh: 他们的公寓里塞满了

sentences.en: I'm still often vain.
sentences.zh: 我依然常常虚荣。

sentences.en: My outlook on life is utterly and completely wrong at present.
sentences.zh: 目前我对生活的看法完全是错误透顶的。

sentences.en: Life is so difficult and so full of sadness around me, and I have so little courage.
sentences.zh: 生活是如此艰难，周围充满了悲伤，而我的勇气又是如此之少。

sentences.en: Over the next weeks, dressed in mourning, she settled into her new home.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，她身着丧服，在新家安顿下来。

sentences.en: She unpacked linens and silverware, met her neighbors, and prepared the house for guests, all the while caring for little Vincent.
sentences.zh: 她打开亚麻布和银器的包裹，结识邻居，为客人准备房子，同时照顾小文森特。

sentences.en: She seems to have spent the greatest amount of her settling-in time, months, in fact, deciding precisely where to hang her brother-in-law's paintings.
sentences.zh: 她似乎花了绝大部分安顿的时间——事实上长达数月——来精确决定在哪里悬挂她小叔子的画作。

sentences.en: Eventually, virtually every inch of wall space was covered with them.
sentences.zh: 最终，几乎每一寸墙壁空间都挂满了这些画。

sentences.en: The potato eaters, the large, mostly brown, study of peasants at a humble meal that scholars consider Vincent's first masterpiece, was hung above the fireplace.
sentences.zh: 《吃土豆的人》——这幅学者们认为是文森特第一部杰作的大型、主要呈棕色的平民简朴餐食研究画作——被挂在了壁炉上方。

sentences.en: She festooned her bedroom with three canvases depicting orchards in vibrant bloom.
sentences.zh: 她用三幅描绘生机勃勃盛开果园的画布装点她的卧室。

sentences.en: One of her guests later remarked that the whole house was filled with Vincent's.
sentences.zh: 她的一位客人后来评论说，整个房子里都充满了文森特的痕迹。

sentences.en: Once all was more or less the way she wanted it.
sentences.zh: 一旦一切或多或少达到了她想要的样子，

sentences.en: She picked up one of the lined notebooks and returned to the diary she began in her teens.
sentences.zh: 她拿起一本带线笔记本，重新开始写她十几岁时开始的日记。

sentences.en: She set it aside the moment she started her life with Teo.
sentences.zh: 从她开始与特奥生活的那一刻起，她就把日记放在了一边。

sentences.en: Her last entry, from almost exactly three years before, began,
sentences.zh: 她几乎正好在三年前的最后一篇日记开头写道：

sentences.en: On Thursday morning, I go to Paris.
sentences.zh: 星期四早上，我去巴黎。

sentences.en: During the whole mad period that followed, she was too busy to keep a journal, too swept up in another life.
sentences.zh: 在接下来疯狂的整个时期里，她忙得没空记日记，完全被另一种生活席卷进去了。

sentences.en: Now she was back.
sentences.zh: 现在她回来了。

sentences.en: It's all nothing but a dream, she wrote from her guest house.
sentences.zh: 这一切不过是一场梦，她在客房里写道。

sentences.en: What lies behind me, my short, blissful, marital happiness, that, too, has been a dream.
sentences.zh: 留在我身后的，我短暂而幸福的婚姻生活，那也曾是一场梦。

sentences.en: For a year and a half, I was the happiest woman on earth.
sentences.zh: 有一年半的时间，我是世界上最幸福的女人。

sentences.en: Then, matter-of-factly, she identified the two responsibilities that Teo had given her.
sentences.zh: 然后，她实事求是地指出了特奥交给她的两项责任。

sentences.en: As well as the child, she wrote, he has left me another task, Vincent's work, getting it seen and appreciated as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 除了孩子，她写道，他还留给我另一项任务，那就是文森特的作品，让它尽可能多地被看到和欣赏。

sentences.en: Having no training in how to achieve this, she began with what was at hand.
sentences.zh: 由于没有受过如何实现这一目标的训练，她从手头现有的东西开始做起。

sentences.en: In addition to Vincent's paintings, she had inherited the enormous trove of letters that the brothers had exchanged.
sentences.zh: 除了文森特的画作之外，她还继承兄弟俩通信的大量宝库。

sentences.en: In Bussum, in the evenings, with her guests taken care of and the baby asleep, she poured over them.
sentences.zh: 在比森的夜晚，当客人们安顿好、宝宝睡着后，她便埋头细读这些信件。

sentences.en: Nearly all, it turned out, were from Vincent.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，几乎所有信件都来自文森特。

sentences.en: Her husband had carefully kept Vincent's letters, but Vincent hadn't been so fastidious with the ones his brother had sent him.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫精心保留了文森特的信，但文森特对兄弟寄给他的信却没那么讲究。

sentences.en: Details of the artist's daily life and tribulations, his insomnia, his poverty, his self-doubt, were mixed with accounts of paintings he was working on,
sentences.zh: 这位艺术家日常生活和磨难的细节——他的失眠、他的贫穷、他的自我怀疑——与他正在创作的画作的描述交织在一起，

sentences.en: techniques he experimented with, what he was reading, descriptions of paintings by other artists he drew inspiration from.
sentences.zh: 包括他尝试过的技术、他在读什么书，以及对激发他灵感的其他艺术家画作的描述。

sentences.en: He often felt the need to put into words what he was trying to achieve with color.
sentences.zh: 他经常觉得需要用文字来表达他试图用色彩实现的目标。

sentences.en: Town violet, star yellow, sky blue green, the wheat fields have all the tones, old gold, copper, green gold, red gold, yellow gold, green, red, and yellow bronze.
sentences.zh: 城镇紫、星星黄、天空蓝绿，麦田拥有所有的色调：黄金色、铜色、绿金色、红金色、黄金色、绿色、红色和黄色青铜色。

sentences.en: Repeatedly, he sought to explain his objective in capturing what he was looking at.
sentences.zh: 他多次试图解释自己在捕捉所见之物时的目标。

sentences.en: I tried to reconstruct the thing as it may have been by simplifying and accentuating the proud, unchanging nature of the pines and the cedar bushes against the blue.
sentences.zh: 我试图通过简化和强化松树和雪松灌木丛在蓝色背景下高傲、永恒的本性，来重构那可能存在的事物。

sentences.en: He described his harrowing mental breakdowns and his fear of future collapses, that a more violent crisis may destroy my ability to paint forever,
sentences.zh: 他描述了自己痛苦的精神崩溃以及对未来崩溃的恐惧，担心更猛烈的危机可能会永远摧毁我作画的能力，

sentences.en: and his notion that should he experience another episode, he could go into an asylum or even to the town prison, where there's usually an isolation cell.
sentences.zh: 并且提到如果他再次经历发作，他可以去精神病院，甚至去通常有隔离室的镇监狱。

sentences.en: She did a lot of other reading as well, undertaking what amounted to a self-guided course in art criticism.
sentences.zh: 她还阅读了大量其他书籍，进行了相当于艺术批评的自学课程。

sentences.en: She read the Belgian journal La Moderne, which advocated the idea that art should serve progressive political causes, and took notes.
sentences.zh: 她阅读了比利时杂志《现代》，该杂志主张艺术应该服务于进步的政治事业，并做了笔记。

sentences.en: She read a book of criticism by the Irish novelist George Moore, jotting down a quote from it that seemed pertinent.
sentences.zh: 她读了一本由爱尔兰小说家乔治·穆尔撰写的评论书，并从中记下了一句似乎相关的名言。

sentences.en: The lot of critics is to be remembered by what they failed to understand.
sentences.zh: 评论家的命运往往因他们未能理解的事物而被世人铭记。

sentences.en: As if to steel herself for her task ahead, she also read a biography of one of her heroes,
sentences.zh: 仿佛为了迎接即将到来的任务而让自己坚强起来，她还读了一位她心目中英雄的传记，

sentences.en: Marianne Evans, the English proto-feminist and social critic, who wrote novels under the pen name George Eliot.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安·埃文斯，这位英国早期女权主义者和社会批评家，曾以笔名乔治·艾略特创作小说。

sentences.en: She described Evans in her diary as that great, courageous, intelligent woman whom I've loved and revered almost since childhood,
sentences.zh: 她在日记中将埃文斯描述为那位伟大、勇敢、聪明的女性，自童年起我就一直爱戴和崇敬她，

sentences.en: and noted that remembering her is always an incentive to be better.
sentences.zh: 并指出铭记她始终是变得更好的动力。

sentences.en: She began to circulate in society.
sentences.zh: 她开始在社交界活动。

sentences.en: Some of the people she knew in the area were part of a community of artists, poets, and intellectuals who had founded an arts journal called The New Guide.
sentences.zh: 她在当地认识的一些人属于一个由艺术家、诗人和知识分子组成的社群，他们曾创办一本名为《新导报》的艺术杂志。

sentences.en: As the industrialization of the late 1880s and early 1890s spawned an anarchist movement and rising nationalisms, they were processing the ferment in Western society
sentences.zh: 随着19世纪80年代末和90年代初的工业化催生了无政府主义运动和日益高涨的民族主义，他们正在消化西方社会的激荡，

sentences.en: and sorting through how the arts should respond.
sentences.zh: 并厘清艺术应当如何回应。

sentences.en: Yeo's diary gives the impression of her attending their gatherings and not so much participating in conversations as listening while the intellectuals held forth
sentences.zh: 约的日记给人一种印象，即她出席了他们的聚会，与其说是在参与谈话，不如说是在听着知识分子们高谈阔论

sentences.en: on what was wrong with the art of the classical tradition, which followed prescribed rules and favored idea over emotion and line over color.
sentences.zh: 古典传统艺术哪里出了问题——这种传统遵循规定的规则，青睐思想而非情感，青睐线条而非色彩。

sentences.en: Critics like Josef Albertink Time, professor of aesthetics and the history of art at Amsterdam's State Academy of Visual Arts, held that artists had a moral duty
sentences.zh: 诸如阿姆斯特丹国立视觉艺术学院美学与艺术史教授约瑟夫·阿尔伯丁克·蒂姆等评论家认为，艺术家肩负着道德责任，
zh_words: 约瑟夫·阿尔伯丁克·蒂姆

sentences.en: to uphold Christian ideals that undergirded society and to enhance the representation of nature in a way that must be firm, clear, purified.
sentences.zh: 要维护支撑社会的基督教理想，并以必须坚定、清晰、纯净的方式增强对自然的表现。

sentences.en: By the end of her first year on her own, living with Vincent's paintings and his words, reading deeply, immersing herself from time to time in these gatherings,
sentences.zh: 在独自生活的头一年结束时，她与文森特的画作和文字相伴，进行深度阅读，不时沉浸在这些聚会中，

sentences.en: Yeo had experienced a kind of epiphany.
sentences.zh: 约经历了一种顿悟。

sentences.en: Van Gogh's letters were part and parcel of the art.
sentences.zh: 梵高的书信是其艺术不可分割的一部分。

sentences.en: They were keys to the paintings.
sentences.zh: 它们是理解这些画作的钥匙。

sentences.en: The letters brought the art and the tragic intensely lived life together into a single package.
sentences.zh: 这些书信将艺术以及充满悲剧色彩、被极致体验的生活融为一体。

sentences.en: Yeo would have appreciated the view of the French Impressionists she had met in Paris, that the notion of following rules on how and what to paint
sentences.zh: 约一定会赞同她在巴黎结识的法国印象派画家的观点：即那种认为必须遵循关于如何作画以及画什么的规则的观念

sentences.en: had become impossibly inauthentic, that in a world lacking a central authority, an artist had to look within for guidance.
sentences.zh: 已经变得极其不真实，在一个缺乏中央权威的世界里，艺术家必须向内寻求指导。

sentences.en: That was what Monet, Gauguin, and the others had done, and the results were to be seen on their canvases.
sentences.zh: 这就是莫奈、高更和其他人所做的事情，其结果在他们的画布上一览无遗。

sentences.en: Bringing an artist's biography into the mix was simply another step in the same direction.
sentences.zh: 将艺术家的传记纳入其中，不过是朝同一方向迈出的又一步。

sentences.en: The letters also pointed to the audience
sentences.zh: 这些信件还指向了

sentences.en: Vincent had intended.
sentences.zh: 文森特所设想的受众。

sentences.en: Vincent, who once sought a career as a minister and lived among peasants to humble himself, had desperately wanted to make art that reached beyond the cognoscenti
sentences.zh: 文森特曾一度寻求成为一名牧师，并生活在农民中间以使自己保持谦卑，他极其渴望创作出能够超越行家、

sentences.en: and directly into the hearts of common people.
sentences.zh: 直击普通人内心的艺术。

sentences.en: No result of my work would be more agreeable to me, he wrote to Teo, quoting another artist, than that ordinary working men should hang such prints in their room or workplace.
sentences.zh: 他在引用另一位艺术家的话写给特奥的信中说，我的作品没有任何结果会比普通工人在他们的房间或工作场所挂上这样的版画更让我感到高兴。

sentences.en: Vincent's letters and paintings seemed to reinforce Yeo's own longstanding convictions about social justice.
sentences.zh: 文森特的书信和画作似乎巩固了约长期以来关于社会正义的信念。

sentences.en: As a girl, influenced by Sunday sermons, she longed for a life of purpose.
sentences.zh: 作为一个少女，受星期日布道的熏陶，她渴望过上有意义的生活。

sentences.en: Just before agreeing to marry Teo, she visited Belgium.
sentences.zh: 就在同意嫁给特奥之前，她访问了比利时。

sentences.en: And the minister whose family she was staying with took her to see the living conditions of workers at a nearby coal mine.
sentences.zh: 她寄居其家的那位牧师带她去参观了附近煤矿工人的生活条件。

sentences.en: The experience shook her and helped fuel what became a lifelong dedication to causes, ranging from workers' rights to female suffrage.
sentences.zh: 这段经历震撼了她，并助长了她一生对各项事业的奉献，这些事业从劳工权利延伸到女性选举权。

sentences.en: She counted herself as one of the ordinary people
sentences.zh: 她把自己算作是文森特

sentences.en: Vincent had written of, and she knew that he had considered himself one as well.
sentences.zh: 曾写过的普通人之一，并且她知道文森特也认为自己是其中之一。

sentences.en: After consuming her tortured brother-in-law's words alone in her guesthouse one night during a storm in 1891, with the wind howling outside, she wrote in a letter,
sentences.zh: 1891年暴风雨交加的一个夜晚，独自坐在宾馆里读完她饱受折磨的姐夫留下的文字，听着窗外的呼啸狂风，她在信中写道：

sentences.en: I felt so desolate that for the first time I understood what he must have felt in those times when everyone turned away from him.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如此孤独，以至于生平第一次明白了，每当所有人背弃他时，他当时内心会有怎样的感受。

sentences.en: She was now ready to act as agent for Vincent van Gogh.
sentences.zh: 如今，她已经准备好担任文森特·梵高的经纪人了。

sentences.en: One of her first moves was to approach an art critic named Jan Vett, who in addition to being the husband of a friend was at the forefront of the new guide's circle.
sentences.zh: 她的第一步行动之一就是接触一位名叫扬·韦特的艺术评论家，此人不仅是一位朋友的丈夫，也处于新艺术圈子的前沿。

sentences.en: Vett was outspoken in his rejection of academic art and in promoting individual expression.
sentences.zh: 韦特直言不讳地反对学院派艺术，并积极推崇个性表达。

sentences.en: At first, though,
sentences.zh: 然而起初，

sentences.en: Vett dismissed Vincent's work outright and belittled Yeo's efforts.
sentences.zh: 韦特对文森特的作品不屑一顾，并贬低乔的努力。

sentences.en: He himself later admitted that he was initially repelled by the raw violence of some van Goghs and found these paintings nearly vulgar.
sentences.zh: 他自己后来也承认，起初他曾被某些梵高作品中原始的暴力感所排斥，觉得这些画作近乎粗俗。

sentences.en: His reaction, despite his commitment to the new, gives a sense of the shock that Vincent's canvases engendered at first sight.
sentences.zh: 尽管他致力于新潮艺术，但他的反应却体现了文森特的画作在初见时所引发的震撼。

sentences.en: Another early critic found Vincent's landscapes without depth, without atmosphere, without light, the unmixed colors set beside each other without mutually harmonizing,
sentences.zh: 另一位早期评论家认为，文森特的风景画缺乏深度、缺乏氛围、缺乏光感，未调和的色彩并列在一起却互不协调，

sentences.en: and complained that the artist was painting out of a desire to be modern, bizarre, childlike.
sentences.zh: 并抱怨这位艺术家作画是出于追求现代、离奇和幼稚。

sentences.en: Yeo found Vett's reaction disappointingly conventional.
sentences.zh: 乔发现韦特的反应令人失望地墨守成规。

sentences.en: He must also have said something disparaging about a woman seeking to enter the art world, because she complained to her diary after an encounter with him.
sentences.zh: 他也一定说过一些贬低女性涉足艺术界的话，因为她在与他见面后向日记抱怨道：

sentences.en: We women are for the most part what men want us to be.
sentences.zh: 我们女性在很大程度上只是男人希望我们成为的样子。

sentences.en: But she realized his importance as a critic and believed that his openness to new ideas meant that she could persuade him to appreciate the paintings, telling her diary,
sentences.zh: 但她意识到了他作为评论家的重要性，并相信他对新思想的开放态度意味着她可以劝说他欣赏这些画作，她在日记中写道：

sentences.en: I won't rest until he likes them.
sentences.zh: 在让他喜欢上它们之前，我绝不罢休。

sentences.en: She pressed an envelope full of Vincent's letters on Vett, encouraging him to use them as she had as a means to illuminate the paintings.
sentences.zh: 她将装满文森特书信的信封塞给韦特，鼓励他像她一样将其作为阐释这些画作的途径。

sentences.en: She didn't try to come across like an art critic, but instead poured her heart out to the man, trying to guide him toward the shift in thinking that she felt was needed to perceive
sentences.zh: 她没有试图表现得像个艺术评论家，而是向这个人倾注了心血，试图引导他实现她认为必不可少的思维转变，从而去感知

sentences.en: a new mode of artistic expression.
sentences.zh: 一种全新的艺术表达模式。

sentences.en: She explained to Vett that she had begun reading the correspondence between the brothers in order to be closer to her dead husband, but then Vincent stole his way into her.
sentences.zh: 她向韦特解释说，为了离已故的丈夫更近，她开始阅读兄弟俩的通信，但随后文森特却走进了她的内心。

sentences.en: I read the letters not only with my head, I was deep into them with my whole soul, she wrote to Vett.
sentences.zh: 她写信给韦特：“我读这些信不仅是用理智，我用整个灵魂深深地沉浸其中。”

sentences.en: I read them and re-read them until the whole figure of Vincent was clear before me.
sentences.zh: “我一遍又一遍地读，直到文森特的整个形象清晰地展现在我眼前。”

sentences.en: She told him that she wished she could make you feel the influence that Vincent has had on my life.
sentences.zh: 她告诉他，她希望自己能“让你感受到文森特对我的生活产生的影响”。

sentences.en: I've found serenity.
sentences.zh: “我找到了平静。”

sentences.en: Her timing was good,
sentences.zh: 她出现得正是时候，

sentences.en: The Dutch historian
sentences.zh: 荷兰历史学家

sentences.en: Johan Hausinga later characterized the change of spirit that began to be felt in art and literature around 1890 as a swirl of ideas that coalesced around two poles,
sentences.zh: 约翰·赫伊津哈后来将1890年前后开始在艺术和文学中感受到的精神变革，描述为围绕两个极点汇聚的思潮漩涡，

sentences.en: that of socialism and that of mysticism.
sentences.zh: 即社会主义极与神秘主义极。

sentences.en: Jo saw that Vincent's art straddled both.
sentences.zh: 乔看出文森特的艺术兼跨了这两者。

sentences.en: Jan Vett was among those trying to process a shift from impressionism to something new, an art that applied individualism to social and even spiritual questions.
sentences.zh: 扬·韦特正是那些试图适应从印象派向新事物转变的人之一，这种艺术将个人主义应用于社会甚至精神问题。

sentences.en: He listened to Jo and came around.
sentences.zh: 他听取了乔的意见并转变了立场。

sentences.en: He wrote one of the first appreciations of the artist, saying that he now saw the astonishing clairvoyance of great humility and characterized Vincent as an artist who seeks
sentences.zh: 他写下了最早对这位艺术家的赞赏文章之一，称他现在看到了伟大谦逊中所蕴含的惊人先见之明，并将文森特描述为一位探求

sentences.en: the raw root of things.
sentences.zh: 事物原始根源的艺术家。
